## Claims
- [computed] For \(J=[333,5^5]\subset\Lambda/I_{5,5}\), \(Q=J/A_+J\) has free ranks \((1,1,2,2,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0)\) in degrees \(9,\ldots,25\), with no torsion in those degrees. [artifact b5658ec18b84ad470751544a752f238dadd447fb7b1122a89a299a79e024042f]
- [computed] Thus, for this one case, \(\operatorname{Hilb}_Q(z)=z^9(1+z+2z^2+2z^3+2z^4+z^5+z^6)=z^9\binom52_z\). [artifact b5658ec18b84ad470751544a752f238dadd447fb7b1122a89a299a79e024042f]
- [source-backed] The lower-adjoined Schur family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
- [proved] If homogeneous ideal generators \(G\) have \(\mathbb Z\)-linearly independent images in \(J/A_+J\), then their images form a homogeneous \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J/A_+J\).
- [proved] Irredundant ideal generation does not imply integral independence in indecomposables: for \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\) and \(J=(2x,x^2)\), the irredundant set \(\{2x,x^2\}\) has \(J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2\).

## Strategy
Use the indecomposable-basis lemma. Since \(G\) generates \(J\), its residues generate \(Q=J/A_+J\) over \(A/A_+=\mathbb Z\). If they are independent, they are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis; hence \(Q\) is torsion-free and its graded Hilbert series is \(\sum_{g\in G}z^{\deg g}\).

For \((a,b)=(2,3)\), this enumerator is \(z^9\binom52_z\), matching the accepted finite computation. The requested computed-case target is established, but no general integral certificate is claimed.

## Gaps
The unresolved issue is a uniform integral independence/primitivity proof for the displayed generator residues. Minimality, even though source-backed, does not supply it: in the microcase, \(A_+J=(2x^2,x^3)\), so the class of \(x^2\) has order \(2\) in \(J/A_+J\).

Thus the original general torsion-freeness/free-indecomposables certificate is not established.

## Next
No further large computation is warranted; the discriminating missing step is an integral primitivity argument for generator residues.
